shared_elements: tall vertical rectangular slab carved in low relief
raised rounded contour lines with smooth flat ground
horizontal band of repeated zigzag/chevron pattern
row of repeated arch- or crescent-shaped curved motifs
stacked registers reading top to bottom
limbs/appendages ending in splayed digits or claws
radiating fringe of parallel lines (around head in A, at base in A; comparable linear hatching in B)
justification: Both are tall, narrow slabs worked in shallow relief with rounded raised outlines, organised into stacked horizontal registers that include a band of zigzag/chevron ornament and a repeating row of arched or crescentic curved forms near the top. The decisive difference is subject: A is dominated by a single frontal anthropomorphic figure with radiating head and outstretched limbs, whereas B carries several separate profile animals (quadrupeds, birds, serpentine forms) with no central human figure, so the correspondence is limited to format, technique and a few generic motifs.
